exposure: maternal characteristics (race, parity, maternal age, military status, military rank, marital status, birth complications)
cohort: The cohort consisted of 1,463 maternal-infant dyads from a single military medical center who gave birth between March and August in 2019 and 2020.
finding: Overall breastfeeding initiation rates did not significantly differ during the COVID-19 pandemic (2020) compared to the previous year (2019).
mod_finding: Women who gave birth via cesarean section were less likely to initiate breastfeeding, and cesarean birth significantly impacted the breastfeeding initiation model in 2020.
cross-section timing: Data compiled from birthing event health records from March to August in 2019 and 2020.
gest_age: The study included babies of various gestational ages, with those born at 32-37 weeks being less likely to initiate breastfeeding.
